threats.label: What’s at stake
title: What waiting costs.
What waiting
costs.
threats.lead: The threats and potential losses if {brand} doesn’t invest in the next era of its brand.

head: A competitor rebrands
and takes your place.
A competitor rebrands
and takes your place.
items.body: A rival with a sharper brand can launch tomorrow and claim the spot you thought was yours. Markets remember the brand they can describe in one sentence, and it doesn’t have to be the one with the better product.

head: You end up competing
on price.
You end up competing
on price.
items.body: When people can’t tell brands apart, they compare features and price. Without a clear position, every discount becomes your argument.

head: Your fans can’t
explain you.
Your fans can’t
explain you.
items.body: People recommend what they can put into words. If your best customers can’t say what you stand for, word of mouth stays small.

head: Someone else names
your category.
Someone else names
your category.
items.body: If you don’t say what you stand for, a competitor will say it for you, and you’ll spend years correcting their version.

process.label: What happens next
title: What happens next.
What happens
next.
process.lead: Every step up to and including the presentation is free, with no obligation. If a territory fits, the paid work is a brand positioning project built on it.

steps.name: Branding analysis
steps.body: This read of {brand}. You have it now.

steps.name: Questionnaire
steps.body: If it’s useful, you answer a short questionnaire about where you want {brand} to go.

steps.name: Curated territories
steps.body: From your answers we design a few territories: different directions for how {brand} could look, sound and stand.

steps.name: Presentation
steps.body: We present the territories to your team, live.

questionnaire.title: {brand} questionnaire
questionnaire.intro: A few questions about where you want {brand} to go. It takes about seven minutes, and we use your answers to design the creative territories.

steps.q: Which brands do you admire, and which are not for {brand}?
steps.hint: Tap once for love, twice for not for us. Add any brand that’s missing.
Drag each one. The middle means you don’t mind.

steps.q: Pick up to three words {brand} should be.
steps.hint: Then, if you like, the ones it should never be.

steps.q: What can {brand} do that its competitors can’t?
steps.hint: The thing you’d say first in a pitch.

steps.q: In 12 months, what has to be true for this to have worked?
steps.hint: A business result, not a design one.

steps.q: Who do you want {brand} to be compared to?
steps.hint: Brands in or outside your category.
steps.placeholder: For example: Apple Health, Strava, Aesop

steps.q: In one sentence, what should people say about {brand}?
steps.hint: Write it the way a customer would say it to a friend.
Colors, words, references, things you’ve already tried. Optional.

steps.q: Who else should see the territories?

questionnaire.contactQ: Where should we send the territories?
questionnaire.done: Thank you. We’ll start on the territories and reach out to set up the presentation.
questionnaire.privacy: We save your name, email and answers in our CRM to prepare the territories, and we measure which steps are completed. We never sell them or use them for ads.
